2609.20541.title: An Analysis of Training-Free Self-Reported Confidence in Language Models
2609.20541.paper_summary: Large language models can report a numerical confidence together with generated content, but it is unclear whether this report is more than calibrated rhetoric. We analyze three training-free signals: confidence verbalized with the answer, post-hoc $P(\mathrm{True})$, and agreement with three additional generations on the same 100 TriviaQA questions for two model families. Direct verbalization is a surprisingly strong baseline: after auditing benchmark errors, it reaches AUROC 0.956 and 0.937 for correctness prediction. Three-sample agreement is substantially weaker (0.765 and 0.790), and a fixed interpolation with verbalized confidence has no statistically reliable benefit. Four of nine errors from one model and two of eight from the other receive unanimous sample support, showing that self-consistency can amplify shared misconceptions. Re-eliciting confidence for the same fixed answers with equivalent prompts changes scores by 0.043 to 0.084 on average and flips 4\% to 9\% of decisions at a 0.8 threshold. An exploratory audit of 100 confidence-tagged biography claims further finds only a modest confidence gap between supported and contradicted claims. These results argue that useful self-reports remain sensitive to elicitation, correlated errors, and benchmark noise.
2609.20541.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型可以在生成內容的同時報告數值信心，但尚不清楚這種報告是否僅僅是經過校準的修辭。我們分析了三種無需訓練的信號：用答案表達的信心、事後的 $P(\mathrm{True})$，以及對同一 100 個 TriviaQA 問題的三次額外生成的協議，針對兩個模型系列。直接的口頭表達是一個令人驚訝的強基線：在審核基準錯誤後，其正確性預測達到 AUROC 0.956 和 0.937。三樣本協議明顯較弱（0.765 和 0.790），而用口頭表達的信心進行固定插值則沒有統計上可靠的好處。來自一個模型的九個錯誤中有四個和來自另一個模型的八個錯誤中有兩個獲得一致的樣本支持，顯示自我一致性可以放大共同的誤解。對於相同的固定答案，使用等效提示重新引出信心，平均改變分數 0.043 到 0.084，並在 0.8 的閾值下翻轉 4\% 到 9\% 的決策。對 100 個信心標記的傳記聲明進行的探索性審核進一步發現，支持與反駁聲明之間的信心差距僅為適度。這些結果表明，有用的自我報告仍然對引出、相關錯誤和基準噪聲敏感。
